study.title: Altered functional brain activity in first-episode major depressive disorder treated with electro-acupuncture: A resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (electro-acupuncture stimulation vs sham-acupuncture stimulation); resting-state fMRI pre- and post-treatment
study.randomization: Patients with first-episode MDD randomly divided into EAS group and SAS group
study.blinding: Not explicitly described beyond sham procedure; no formal blinding assessment reported
study.population: 28 right-handed first-episode MDD patients enrolled from Guang'anmen Hospital, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences
study.inclusion_criteria: Diagnosis assessed by experienced psychiatrists with DSM-V criteria; HAMD-24 ≥ 20; age 18–60 years; right-handed; first-episode MDD
study.exclusion_criteria: Severe chronic medical or neurological diseases; bipolar disorder; anxiety disorder or other mental disorders; risk of suicide; drug or alcohol addicts; contraindications to MRI scanning; psychiatric drugs, cognitive behavioral therapy, and other complementary and alternative treatments during the treatment

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needles are explicitly inserted into the 'superficial area' of the acupoints with no manipulation performed. This indicates skin-level only insertion (cutaneous, not reaching muscle/fascia), consistent with Level 2 superficial needling.

Identical sham protocol to SAS_pre: needles inserted into the 'superficial area' of the same acupoints with no manipulation. This describes skin-level penetration only, consistent with Level 2 superficial needling.

interventions.treatment_period_exact: 6 weeks (3 times one week, every other day)

extraction_notes.note: The HAMA-14 group × time interaction F-value and P-value are inconsistently reported. Table 2 shows F = 5.103, P = 0.023, while the text in Section 3.2 states F = 5.103, P = 0.032. Both values are preserved; the discrepancy is flagged.

No sensory, deqi, or blinding/expectancy measures were reported or administered. Neither MASS, VAS for sensation, nor any other deqi instrument was used. This is not stated explicitly but is inferable from the absence of any such data in the paper.
No adverse events data were reported in the paper. The paper does not state whether adverse events were monitored or whether any occurred.
The scanner field strength (Tesla) is not explicitly reported. The scanner is identified as 'Siemens Medical, Erlangen, Germany' but no field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T) is stated.
No blinding assessment was performed or reported. The paper does not describe how participants were blinded or whether they correctly guessed their treatment allocation.

The paper states 'we divided 28 patients...into 14 each in the EAS group and SAS groups' and uses the phrase 'four groups' throughout the results. The 'four groups' refers to EAS_pre, EAS_post, SAS_pre, SAS_post (i.e., two arms × two timepoints), not four distinct groups. This is confirmed by context but may cause confusion.

Figure 3 shows P-values for post hoc comparisons (P=0.027, P=0.032, P<0.01, P=0.012) extracted from figure labels, but these are not fully tabulated in the main text. Values were extracted from figure captions and figure labels.
Figure 5 shows P-values for post hoc FC comparisons (P<0.01, P=0.042) extracted from figure labels. These are not fully tabulated in the main text. Values were extracted from figure.
The paper does not report the EAS instrument manufacturer beyond 'Hua Tuo brand electronic acupuncture instrument SDZ-V'. Needle type, gauge, and depth are not reported for either group.

No within-group change statistics (e.g., pre vs post t-test for individual groups on HAMD/HAMA) are formally reported. Only the group × time interaction and post hoc between-group comparisons are stated.

The paper states 'In the EAS group...a positive correlation between the change in FC of the left MTG and left MFG and the change in HAMD-24 score (r = 0.539, P = 0.047)'. The direction interpretation: a positive correlation between FC change and HAMD-24 change means greater increase in FC is associated with greater decrease (improvement) in HAMD-24. However, the sign of HAMD-24 change (as decrease or raw value) is not fully clarified.

The paper references supplementary data ('Supplementary data to this article can be found online at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2024.e29613') but no supplementary material was provided for extraction.
The paper does not report drop-outs or number of completers per arm. It enrolls and randomizes 28 and appears to analyze 28 (14 per arm) without reporting attrition.

The paper states 'No manipulation was performed during the entire treatment, thus not DE Qi was obtained from the acupuncture points' in the SAS group. This is a description of intended absence of deqi; actual patient-reported sensations in the SAS group are not assessed or reported.
